To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the FEM simulation of a reflection differential pencil probe scanning a surface notch in aluminium is in a good agreement with the experimental measurements of its impedance variations, and (2) the simulation results of the absolute coil scanning the surface notch in aluminium are in good agreement with the impedance data taken from literature

“The FEM model of a reflection differential surface pencil probe, with a split-D coil and an additional coil for the excitation, can successfully predict the impedance variations when the probe scans surface notches in conductive materials.”
the FEM simulation results for the reflection differential split-D sensor scanning surface notches in aluminum are in good agreement with the experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of FEM simulation models for reflection differential split-D probes, which are used for the inspection of surface notches in aluminum.
the FEM simulation of a surface differential eddy current probe scanning a surface notch in 3-D half-space.
the simulation of the interaction of an absolute and a differential split-D eddy current probe with a surface notch in a conductive half-space.

, in order to obtain reliable results for a differential split-D eddy current probe, a maximum mesh size of 2.5mm, a mesh distribution of 10 and an extent of the surrounding 3-D air domain equal to the probe length (Lp=20mm) are recommended.
the FEM is capable of modelling the interaction of a differential probe with a surface notch in a 3-D half-space with a high degree of accuracy.
the simulation results are valid for the case of the differential probe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simulation results for the reflection differential probe are more reliable than those for the absolute probe.

FEM modelling is a viable alternative for the design and development of eddy current probes, especially when the probe is complex and the design of its analytical model is not possible or very challenging.
FEM is a powerful tool for the numerical modelling of differential eddy current sensors and the results of our study may be useful for future researchers in this field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 3-D FEM simulation can be a useful tool for the design and development of differential probes.
FEM can reliably be used to predict the behaviour of differential probes in detecting and sizing surface notches.
the simulated impedance data of the differential probe closely follow the experimental data.
